I will tell you only that beside the last line, the empty one, the one for our children, he wrote: *"We shall see."*

He took the black carnation from his buttonhole and pinned it on my lapel, with cold hands. "I have worn it since 1828," he said. "Now it is your turn. It is a flower that does not wither." I wear it still. It has never withered.
